excerpt_catalog: Sources follow supplied-original order; offsets are Unicode positions. Previews locate text, not evidence. Exact repeats within one source share its first anchor; all occurrences remain in the original. Anchors prove transcription, not an occurrence's applicability, scope or completeness. Put a supplied [[original:ID]] alone in an unindented top-level content paragraph, outside code/HTML, lists and blockquotes; the program copies the whole block. Other fences must be closed standalone blocks reproducing a complete supplied block or original fenced example, including prefixes, comments and values. Carry the selected occurrence's adjacent conditions and operation stage; window-edge blocks may be partial. Do not reconstruct commands or table alignment from extraction line breaks. Explain lost alignment locally. Standalone inline file paths must occur verbatim in supplied text. Native table coordinates must match qualified source metadata. Metadata stays ordinary prose.
excerpt_references: Select supplied reference IDs in excerpt parts; the program copies original bytes. Refs identify transcription and source positions, not applicability or a complete procedure. Keep necessary conditions in prose. Derived path templates need refs to at least two concrete examples; never describe a template as an original quote.
summary_task:
Turn each supplied original section into a usable reference section.
For each operation or object, carry its applicability and prerequisites together
with its steps, parameters, alternatives, exceptions and results. Cover requirements
stated only once, including those without a planned concept page. Combine repetition
within the same scope; retain separate variants when their conditions differ.

Use explanatory prose for meaning, and the original excerpt catalog for command or
configuration syntax: select its complete supplied block instead of rewriting it.
Keep standalone paths from prose or complete qualified native cells in inline code
with exact original spelling. Do not put a decoded table cell or path in a new code
fence; use the complete original table excerpt when preserving its syntax, including
its HTML tags and entity encoding. Preserve every token, prefix and comment marker
in each quoted line. A quoted template remains a template. When extraction has split a command or
lost table alignment, retain the readable fragment and identify that specific
structural gap; a reconstructed executable command or column assignment needs
explicit support. Reproduce reliably aligned tables with their object and condition
headers. Keep page/section boundaries and cross-references visible where they affect
interpretation. Preceding context supplies conditions, not extra primary ranges.

Include explanations, comparisons and source-supported calculations with their
premises. Each paragraph should explain or preserve the supplied section, without
adding unrelated advice or expanding a local observation to the entire document.
Return one JSON object in this complete shape:
{"description": "brief document description", "sections":
 [{"id": "the supplied output section id", "content": "complete Markdown knowledge"}]}.
Return every output_sections id exactly once, retaining its original requirements,
conditions and useful explanation in the corresponding body, not only its heading.
Use the document's necessary level of detail without a fixed compression ratio.
Return JSON without an outer code fence or frontmatter. Markdown code fences inside
section content are appropriate for exact technical excerpts.
Place each [[original:ID]] in an unindented top-level paragraph with blank lines
around it. Do not put excerpt references in numbered lists, bullets or blockquotes.

concept_page:
Write the concept page for: {title}

This concept relates to the original document "{doc_name}" supplied above.
{update_instruction}

Return one JSON object containing these page fields and any required source_ranges:
- "description": A single sentence (under 100 chars) describing this topic as documented
- "source_ranges": When requested, the supplied range IDs used by the final body,
  in the same object as description and content
- "content": A reference page covering this topic's relevant original sections.
  Organize by operation or object: keep prerequisites and applicable variants with
  their steps, parameter values, exceptions and results. Include the conditions
  needed to use each operation, even when mentioned only once or on an adjacent
  page. Quote technical syntax verbatim in fenced excerpts; preserve prefixes,
  comment markers and the difference between a template and an executable command.
  Explain supported relationships and derivations with their premises. Keep sparse
  sources concise. Links provide navigation; the application appends source and
  related-page links. Use the whitelist for supported relationships in prose.

Return ONLY valid JSON, no fences.
